newsitem.title: UKRAINE: ATHLETICS-INJURED BUBKA TO MISS HIS HOME EVENT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-INJURED BUBKA TO MISS HIS HOME EVENT.

text.p: World pole vault champion Sergei Bubka is to miss a big event he organised in his home town because of an Achilles tendon injury that forced him to quit last year's Olympics.

"His doctor has banned him from jumping. He will stay out of competition for at least two months, maybe more," Lyubov Mishchenko, who helped organise Sunday's event in Ukraine's eastern industrial city of Donetsk, said on Thursday.

The holder of 35 world records over 13 years will be reduced to acting as host of Sunday's "Pole-Stars" international indoor competition in Donetsk, where he is viewed as a hero and fans were dreaming he would leap to new heights.
Mishchenko said Olympic gold pole vaulter Jean Galfione and Germany's bronze medal winner Andrej Tiwontschik would attend.
An offical at Bubka's sports club said the 32-year-old athlete was travelling to Finland once a month to consult his doctors, and he would act as commentator on Sunday.

Bubka plunged his coal-mining home town into dispair when he had to quit his event at the Atlanta Games last July with the Achilles injury. He had been warming up for the final with the bar set at 5.70 metres.
Bubka said at the time his injury was "like fire" and warned it might finish his career.
